To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of metrics for project analysis is a common practice in software organizations; (b) project managers often ask the same type of queries about projects; (c) the use of a conceptual framework for project queries and metrics facilitates the process of project analysis; (d) the use of the WWW as a medium to formulate and display queries is a promising approach; and (e) the use of heuristics to evaluate queries can be used to provide more accurate results.

the use of a conceptual model for the formulation of project management queries and the development of a framework that can be used by both technical and non-technical experts to formulate and analyze queries can lead to a more systematic, informed approach to project management.
the F-metric framework can be used by project managers to pose and answer project management queries using software metrics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a flexible, extensible, intelligent framework for formulating and evaluating project management queries in the context of software metrics, and providing an interface to display results in the form of a graphical dashboard.
providing a conceptual framework and a tool to help software organizations formulate, analyze and manage software metrics.

the following issues: (1) the identification of the types of queries that project managers ask during project execution; (2) the identification of a core set metrics that can be used to answer such queries; (3) the formulation of project queries at a higher level of abstraction than raw metrics; (4) the design and implementation of a flexible framework to answer queries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed an intelligent and flexible framework that allows project managers to formulate and update their queries, and technical experts to modify the evaluation of those queries, without any need for code modification.
our approach is a novel and effective method to support project managers in answering their queries about the progress and status of software projects.
our framework provides a mechanism for intelligent formulation, analysis and display of management queries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a framework which allows managers to formulate project management queries, experts to update heuristics and display results, and both managers and experts to collaborate in the development of the framework.
we developed a conceptual model for software project metrics and defined a query language to express queries about the project in a manner that is understandable to the managers.
our tool provides the flexibility to define, update and display management queries and their solutions in the form of software metrics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a conceptual model of project metrics, a query language, and a flexible WWW-based tool can be used to help project managers make better decisions based on software metrics.

we provide an easy-to-use tool that can be utilized by project managers to formulate and answer management queries in a systematic manner, and by experts to update queries, modify heuristic functions, and dynamically change display of results.
we have developed a framework which can be easily adapted to the needs of a particular organization.
